FINDING_A_THE_OUTAGE.blast_radius: Fleet-wide. Every agent, every bash mcp_call, every cron preflight, both dispatchers. The gateway itself is HEALTHY (see Finding B proof) — only the downstream is dead.

FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.claim: scripts/agents-flow/mcp-call.sh's mcp_call() advertises 2-URL resilience: primary http://localhost:3000/mcp, failover https://zenmidi.com/vn-market/mcp. The failover is NOT vn-market. It is the GATEWAY. It cannot serve any vn-market tool, and never could.
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.proof_1_identity: initialize against the failover URL returns instructions: 'This server is a gateway / proxy in front of m...' — that is the gateway's own instructions string, not vn-market's.
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.proof_2_tool_surface: tools/call name=task_list_held on that URL -> {'code':-32602,'message':'unknown tool "task_list_held"'}. The gateway exposes only meta-tools (list_servers / list_server_tools / search_tools / call_tool).
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.proof_3_protocol: It is STATEFUL — requires initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/call with the minted mcp-session-id. mcp_call() posts tools/call bare, by design ('POST to /mcp works STATELESS' per its own header comment).
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.the_irony: mcp-call.sh's OWN header documents this exact error string as the signature of the stateful gateway endpoint, in a comment explaining why mcp_call_gateway_meta() had to be a separate function. The failover URL inside mcp_call() points at precisely the endpoint that comment warns about.
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.consequence: The '2-URL failover' is 1 URL. Whenever localhost:3000 is down — i.e. exactly when failover is supposed to save you — there is no fallback at all. Affects every bash MCP caller fleet-wide: cowork-tick-preflight.sh, dev-team-tick-preflight.sh, coverage-stamp.sh, every agent's bash path.
FINDING_B_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_failover_UR.NOT_a_URL_typo_to_hand_edit: Do not 'fix' this by swapping in another host. The gateway CAN reach vn-market, but only through its call_tool wrapper with a full handshake — that is a different calling convention, not a different string. Any real fix is a code change with an owner, per CLAUDE.md's canonical-URL rule.

FINDING_C_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_error_repor.what: When URL1 fails at transport level and URL2 returns any 2xx, mcp_call() returns URL2's parse error and SILENTLY DISCARDS URL1's last_err.
FINDING_C_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_error_repor.mechanism: In the for-url loop: URL1 curl_rc!=0 sets last_err then continues. URL2 gets HTTP 200, so the 2?? branch runs '_mcp_call_parse ...; return $?' — returning from INSIDE the loop. The final 'echo [mcp-call] ERROR: $last_err' after the loop is never reached.
FINDING_C_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_error_repor.observed_cost_today: The preflight's detail field read 'fire-election claim transport error: ... method "tools/call" is invalid during session initialization'. That message is about an MCP HANDSHAKE. The actual fault was 'primary timed out after 10s, 0 bytes'. It took 6 separate probes to get from the reported error to the real one.
FINDING_C_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_error_repor.why_it_is_deterministic_not_flaky: The gateway always answers 200 with that JSON-RPC error. So whenever the primary is down, the operator is ALWAYS shown the session-init red herring and NEVER shown the timeout. Not intermittent — structural.
FINDING_C_STRUCTURAL_NEW_the_error_repor.remedy_shape: Accumulate per-URL errors and surface all of them, or at minimum prepend last_err when a later URL also fails. One-line-ish, but it is a code change with an owner — filing, not touching.

Worth a readback next tick. Related: feedback_chef_fabricated_publish, feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit.
FINDING_D_EXPOSURE_guaranteed_slot_firer.structural_gap: Layer C has no liveness precondition on the thing every one of its agents depends on. It will keep firing guaranteed slots into a dead MCP every 900s for as long as the outage lasts.
